answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation tied to verifiable work. An agent that wants its claims trusted must lock a ferrous-hard deposit, costly to forge at scale, and earn endorsements over time from peers that have themselves paid to participate. Like a mesa rising above a sable plain, a long-lived reputation stands out against a flood of cheap, freshly minted identities: each new sybil starts with zero history and must spend real money, compute, and waiting time before its votes count.
